reading_template: the strength-dependent combination form (promoter competition, Bothma et al. 2015 eLife 4:e07956 Methods eqs. 7-9, THETA = 0.5 declared and nothing fitted on any pair), run once on the held-out enhancer-enhancer-promoter combinations of Martinez-Ara et al. 2024 (GSE240586, mouse E14tg2a embryonic stem cells): {verdict}; over {n} combinations ({clusters} unordered enhancer pairs, {promoters} promoters) its mean squared error of the measured boost index is {mse} log2 squared, and against each comparator: {per_comparator}. {falsified}
verdict_words: better than every rule lane-combine compared
not better than every rule lane-combine compared
falsifier: The claim that the strength-dependent form is better than the rules lane-combine compared is FALSIFIED unless the form's mean squared error is below EVERY comparator's (no_rule, mean, max, additive_envelope, multiplicative) with the 95% cluster-bootstrap interval of the difference excluding zero. A single comparator it does not beat is enough to falsify it, and a comparator that beats it with its interval excluding zero is reported as 'worse'.
secondary_deciding_nothing: the share of informative combinations above the additive expectation (supra-additive, which no monotone rule of the terms can produce) and below the stronger single (which contradicts every monotone rule, the Bothma snail case lane-combine used), reported as counts and deciding nothing
decisions: the population is Martinez-Ara et al. 2024 (GSE240586), not lane-combine's Bothma pairs, because lane-combine read those outcomes before writing its rule and said so
the form is the opt-in `competition` rule already in runtime/grn.py; the engine is not changed, and a test pins its header and every existing form byte for byte
the one free number per promoter is fixed by declaration, THETA = 0.5, the constant 7d declared (attribution/combine2.THETA); nothing is fitted on any enhancer pair
the singles are the authors' own Boost1 and Boost2 columns, position- and strand-matched, so no reconstruction of a single's effect enters the comparison
the no-rule baseline, the mean, max, the sum_capped/or envelope and the multiplicative form are all scored on the same combinations, so no form is read on a population another cannot reach
theta_source: attribution/combine2.THETA, declared by 7d on 2026-10-10 and committed in `bc9fc7a`; this lane reads it as 0.5 and refuses to run if it differs
data_decision: lane-combine's own five Bothma pairs cannot test this form independently: that lane read their outcomes before writing its rule and recorded that it had. A held-out population exists that it never read, Martinez-Ara et al. 2024 (GSE240586), whose combinations are designed singles and pairs with one baseline per promoter in one assay and one cell context, so the form is tested there instead, with its shape and its one constant fixed beforehand from two other publications.
exploration_preceded_this: stated so that nothing here is read as a blind prediction. Before fixing the form the lane read: lane-combine's census, registration and result (`a6fc5c4`, `7f3e597`, `93caf61`) and their committed reading; runtime/grn.py's four fixed rules and its two opt-in forms; the 7d, 7f and 7h rows of ROADMAP section 5; the Methods and the DATA AVAILABILITY of Martinez-Ara et al. 2024 and that paper's own one-sentence summary of its finding (that enhancer pairs combine near-additively and that weaker promoters can be supra-additive); and from the table itself the design columns, the eight promoter baselines, the control-control rows and the single-enhancer boost indices, which are this test's INPUTS. It read no activity_all value of any enhancer-enhancer row, and none of the authors' own expectation or cooperativity columns (`columns_never_read`). The form's shape is Bothma et al. 2015's and its one constant is 7d's committed THETA; neither was chosen after seeing an outcome of this dataset.
engine_unchanged: runtime/grn.py is an Apache-2.0 engine file and is not edited by this lane: the form is its existing opt-in rule `competition`, and tests/test_strengthform.py pins the file's licence header and every existing form's identity
stop_list_checked: ROADMAP section 5, 'The stop list of 2026-09-27, reinstated': no AlphaGenome request, no deletion request on the 882 blocks, no new biosample, nothing built in area J, nothing on the node model, no fate ceiling, no BioForge calibration

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 36cabe9

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
